Did you always feel the goal was coming? Yeah, we talked about it at halftime. Some  
parts of the performance in the first half were  quite good, but we conceded some soft goals again.
My staff and the players know we have  to do better for the rest of the season  
to avoid getting into situations where we perform  well but still give away goals too easily.
I think in the first half, we didn’t have  enough players in the box, but we spoke  
about it at halftime—what we needed to do and  that we should never give in, never give up.
We had to use the crowd, the atmosphere,  and the way we come together—the fans,  
the players—pushing until the last second of  the game to even try and get the winning goal.
I’m so proud of the character  the team showed today,  
and that will be so important  for the rest of the season.
You had 88% possession in the second half but  just two shots on goal—does that tell a story? 
I think, like always, statistics  show something, but not everything.
The situations were there, but we still have  to get the shot away or make the final pass.
I think we had a lot of situations inside  the box today, but Dundee United also  
defended well—they blocked some shots  and took responsibility in their box.
But we never stopped believing, and  when you keep pushing so many times  
into the opponent’s box, sooner  or later, a goal has to come.
Today, we were close to scoring  even in the last second of the game.
So, I’m proud of the team. Of course,  we’re not happy with the result,  
but when you’re 2-0 down in the first  half, you have to take the positives.
It’s an important point today, given how  the game went in the first half and how  
we reacted to it. That says a lot about this team.
On Kevin’s contribution Yeah, I think if you look at  
his development from the start of the season,  how hard he has worked in the gym and on the  
training pitch since arriving, it’s really nice  to see a player get rewarded for that effort.
He has pushed so hard to get  better and sharper all the time.
There’s a lot of hard work behind that,  and his mentality has been evident on the  
training pitch. Seeing that translate into  results on the pitch makes us really happy.
Has Kevin been doing extra  work himself in the gym? 
Yes, he’s been pushing hard, trying  to get sharper and improve his game.
He’s been working a lot before  and after training sessions,  
and I’m glad to see his hard  work paying off on the pitch.
He wasn’t very effective in the first half—were  you considering taking him off at halftime? 
Yeah, at halftime, I was talking about whether he  
would continue because he wasn’t  as involved in the first half.
But that’s why I’m here as a football  manager and not a TV pundit—because  
football games are long, and things  can change in the second half.
Maybe one day we can switch  roles and see what happens!
Do you know exactly what the issue was with Kevin? Let’s see. We don’t know exactly what it is yet.
He felt something in the last game,  but we couldn’t find anything specific.
We’ll assess him and see how  he recovers in the coming days.
That’s four goals in six games for Kevin—is  he now looking like the striker you  
expected when you signed him? Yeah, goals are one thing,  
but it’s also about how he  contributes in our buildup,  
how he works all over the pitch, and how he  has improved his defensive responsibilities.
He’s taking more responsibility  now, and when you do that well,  
you find yourself in good  scoring opportunities more often.
He’s more involved in the game,  
and that’s why it’s good to see  how connected he is with the team.
I’m happy with what he’s showing right now.
It’s good to have a goal scorer hitting  form at this stage of the season,  
isn’t it? Every game is now really important. 
Yeah, we want everyone to contribute  with goals, not just one player.
But when you have a player with Kevin’s  quality and his calmness inside the box,  
it’s always good for us.
And he keeps arriving in the  right areas, which is crucial.
Should Kevin be in contention for an  international call-up if he keeps scoring? 
I’m not the decision-maker on that, but I’m  happy with what he’s performing right now.
That’s all I’m going to say.
You gave yourselves a mountain to climb  with the soft goals conceded. You very  
nearly climbed that mountain, but what do you  need to do to stop conceding those soft goals? 
Yeah, of course, we talked about  that after the Celtic game as well.
We need to find a way—together with  the players—to identify the breaking  
points in these situations and do better.
It has to be more difficult for teams to create  chances against us in the last part of the season.
I’m always an optimistic person. I believe  in our capacity, and I’m sure we’re going  
to fix this while also continuing to  do the good things we’ve been doing.
You’ve got a break from the league now with the  Scottish Cup—will it be nice to switch focus? 
Yeah, it’s another important game, and  it’s exciting to play at home again.
It’s a big opportunity for us, so  we’re really looking forward to it.
Have you watched much of your next opponent? 
Not yet, but our analytics team—Mark  and his staff—do a really good job.
We’ve been fully focused on this  game against Dundee United, and now  
we’ll turn our attention to the next one.
Thank you. Thank you.
title: Jimmy Thelin Post Match Press Conference | Aberdeen 2-2 Dundee United
